title: KCET 2009 Chemistry
subject: chemistry
source: KEA question paper (copy) + KEA answer key column A1

questions.q: The ore that is concentrated by Froth Floatation process is
questions.chapter: Old syllabus: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Elements
questions.explanation: Froth floatation is used to concentrate sulphide ores; Cinnabar (HgS) is a sulphide ore.

questions.q: The correct set of four Quantum numbers for outermost electron of Potassium (Z = 19) is
questions.explanation: K has configuration [Ar]4s$^1$, so the outermost electron has n=4, l=0, m=0, s=+1/2.

questions.q: A body of mass x kg is moving with a velocity of 100 ms$^{-1}$. Its de Broglie wavelength is $6.62 \times 10^{-35}$m. Hence x is (h = $6.62 \times 10^{-34}$ Js)
questions.explanation: $\lambda = h/(mv) \Rightarrow m = h/(\lambda v) = 6.62\times10^{-34}/(6.62\times10^{-35}\times100) = 0.1$ kg.

questions.q: The correct order of ionisation energy of C, N, O, F is
questions.explanation: N has extra stability from a half-filled 2p$^3$ subshell, so its ionisation energy exceeds O's, giving C < O < N < F.

questions.q: The oxide of an element whose electronic configuration is 1s$^2$ 2s$^2$ 2p$^6$ 3s$^1$ is
questions.explanation: The configuration is of sodium (Na); Na$_2$O, an alkali metal oxide, is basic.

questions.q: The characteristic not related to alkali metal is
options: their ions are isoelectronic with noble gases
questions.explanation: Alkali metals have LOW ionisation energy (easily lose one electron), so 'high ionisation energy' is not a property of alkali metals.

questions.q: Among the following, the compound that contains ionic, covalent and coordinate linkage is
questions.explanation: NH$_4$Cl has covalent N-H bonds, a coordinate bond forming NH$_4^+$ from NH$_3$ and H$^+$, and an ionic bond between NH$_4^+$ and Cl$^-$.

questions.q: A covalent molecule AB$_3$ has pyramidal structure. The number of lone pair and bond pair electrons in the molecule are respectively
questions.explanation: A pyramidal AB$_3$ molecule (like NH$_3$) has 1 lone pair and 3 bond pairs on the central atom.

questions.q: Excess of carbon dioxide is passed through 50 ml of 0.5 M calcium hydroxide solution. After the completion of the reaction, the solution was evaporated to dryness. The solid calcium carbonate was completely neutralised with 0.1 N Hydrochloric acid. The volume of Hydrochloric acid required is (At. mass of calcium = 40)
questions.explanation: Moles Ca(OH)$_2$ = 0.025; evaporation converts any bicarbonate back to 0.025 mol CaCO$_3$. CaCO$_3$ + 2HCl needs 0.05 mol HCl, so volume = 0.05/0.1 = 500 cm$^3$.

questions.q: A bivalent metal has an equivalent mass of 32. The molecular mass of the metal nitrate is
questions.explanation: Atomic mass = equivalent mass $\times$ valency = 64. M(NO$_3$)$_2$ mass = 64 + 2(62) = 188.

questions.q: The r.m.s. velocity of molecules of a gas of density 4 kg m$^{-3}$ and pressure $1.2 \times 10^5$ Nm$^{-2}$ is
0.5 mole of each of H$_2$, SO$_2$ and CH$_4$ are kept in a container. A hole was made in the container. After 3 hours, the order of partial pressures in the container will be
questions.explanation: Effusion rate $\propto 1/\sqrt{M}$, so lighter gases escape faster; the heaviest gas SO$_2$ remains most, then CH$_4$, then H$_2$.

questions.q: The enthalpy of formation of NH$_3$ is $-46$ kJ mol$^{-1}$. The enthalpy change for the reaction: 2NH$_3$(g) $\longrightarrow$ N$_2$(g) + 3H$_2$(g) is
questions.explanation: Reversing and doubling the formation reaction gives $\Delta H$ = $-2\times(-46)$ = +92 kJ.

questions.q: 5 moles of SO$_2$ and 5 moles of O$_2$ are allowed to react. At equilibrium, it was found that 60% of SO$_2$ is used up. If the partial pressure of the equilibrium mixture is one atmosphere, the partial pressure of O$_2$ is
questions.explanation: 3 mol SO$_2$ reacts, consuming 1.5 mol O$_2$; remaining moles: SO$_2$=2, O$_2$=3.5, SO$_3$=3, total=8.5. $p_{O_2} = (3.5/8.5)\times1 \approx 0.41$ atm.

questions.q: 2HI(g) $\rightleftharpoons$ H$_2$(g) + I$_2$(g). The equilibrium constant of the above reaction is 6.4 at 300 K. If 0.25 mole each of H$_2$ and I$_2$ are added to the system, the equilibrium constant will be
questions.explanation: The equilibrium constant depends only on temperature, so it remains 6.4 regardless of the amounts added.

questions.q: Rate of physical adsorption increases with
questions.explanation: Physical adsorption is exothermic, so it is favoured (increases) by decrease in temperature.

questions.q: IUPAC name of (CH$_3$)$_3$CCl
questions.explanation: (CH$_3$)$_3$CCl is named systematically as 2-chloro-2-methylpropane.

questions.q: Lucas test is associated with
questions.explanation: The Lucas test (ZnCl$_2$/conc. HCl) distinguishes primary, secondary and tertiary alcohols by the rate of turbidity formation.

questions.q: An organic compound on heating with CuO produces CO$_2$ but no water. The organic compound may be
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry: Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.explanation: No water is formed only if the compound has no hydrogen; CCl$_4$ contains no H, only C and Cl, so it gives CO$_2$ but no H$_2$O.

questions.q: The condensation polymer among the following is
questions.explanation: Proteins form by condensation (loss of water) between amino acids via peptide bonds; PVC, polyethene and rubber are addition polymers.

questions.q: The order of stability of metal oxides is
questions.chapter: Old syllabus: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Elements
questions.explanation: From the Ellingham diagram, MgO is thermodynamically most stable, followed by Al$_2$O$_3$, Cr$_2$O$_3$, then Fe$_2$O$_3$ least stable (as per KEA key).

questions.q: The temperature of the slag zone in the metallurgy of Iron using blast furnace is
questions.chapter: Old syllabus: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Elements
questions.explanation: The slag formation zone of the blast furnace operates in the 800-1000 °C range (as per KEA key).

questions.q: The function of Fe(OH)$_3$ in the contact process is
questions.explanation: Fe(OH)$_3$ (as a purifier) is used in the Contact Process to remove arsenious oxide impurity from SO$_2$ gas before catalytic oxidation.

questions.q: In which of the following, NH$_3$ is not used?
options: Group reagent for the analysis of IV group basic radical.
Group reagent for the analysis of III group basic radical.
questions.explanation: Nessler's reagent (K$_2$HgI$_4$ in KOH) is used to detect NH$_3$, but does not itself contain or use NH$_3$; the other three uses involve NH$_3$/NH$_4$OH directly.

questions.q: Argon is used
options: in radiotherapy for treatment of cancer
questions.explanation: Argon, being chemically inert, is used as a shielding gas in high-temperature arc welding (e.g. TIG/MIG welding) to protect the molten metal from oxidation by air.

questions.q: The incorrect statement in respect of Chromyl chloride test is
questions.explanation: In the chromyl chloride test, red-orange CrO$_2$Cl$_2$ vapours form and later give yellow lead chromate with lead acetate; free chlorine is not liberated in this test, making that statement incorrect.

questions.q: The magnetic moment of a transition metal ion is $\sqrt{15}$ B.M. Therefore the number of unpaired electrons present in it is
questions.explanation: $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)}$; setting $n(n+2)=15$ gives n = 3 unpaired electrons.

questions.q: The IUPAC name of [Co(NH$_3$)$_5$ONO]$^{2+}$ ion is
questions.explanation: ONO$^-$ bonded through O is nitrito-O; overall charge +2 with 5 neutral NH$_3$ and -1 nitrito gives Co oxidation state +3, so it is pentaamminenitrito-O-cobalt(III) ion.

questions.q: The oxidation state of Fe in the brown ring complex : [Fe(H$_2$O)$_5$NO]SO$_4$ is
questions.explanation: Treating NO as neutral (or as NO$^+$) in this complex is ambiguous by convention, so KEA accepted both +2 (NO neutral) and +1 (NO$^+$) as correct.

questions.q: The correct statement with regard to H$_2^+$ and H$_2^-$ is
options: H$_2^-$ is more stable than H$_2^+$
H$_2^+$ is more stable than H$_2^-$
Both H$_2^+$ and H$_2^-$ are equally stable
Both H$_2^+$ and H$_2^-$ do not exist
questions.explanation: Both have bond order 0.5, but H$_2^-$ has an electron in the antibonding orbital causing extra repulsion, making H$_2^+$ more stable.

questions.q: Arrange the following in the increasing order of their bond order : O$_2$, O$_2^+$, O$_2^-$ and O$_2^{--}$
2 gm of a radioactive sample having half life of 15 days was synthesised on 1$^{st}$ Jan 2009. The amount of the sample left behind on 1$^{st}$ March, 2009 (including both the days)
questions.explanation: The elapsed period (Jan 1 to Mar 1, inclusive) is about 60 days = 4 half-lives, so the sample reduces to $2\times(1/2)^4 = 0.125$ g.

questions.q: For a chemical reaction A $\to$ B, the rate of the reaction is $2 \times 10^{-3}$ mol dm$^{-3}$ s$^{-1}$, when the initial concentration is 0.05 mol dm$^{-3}$. The rate of the same reaction is $1.6 \times 10^{-2}$ mol dm$^{-3}$ s$^{-1}$ when the initial concentration is 0.1 mol dm$^{-3}$. The order of the reaction is
questions.explanation: Rate increases 8-fold when concentration doubles: $2^n=8 \Rightarrow n=3$.

questions.q: For the decomposition of a compound AB at 600 K, the following data were obtained: [AB] 0.20, 0.40, 0.60 mol dm$^{-3}$ give rates $2.75\times10^{-8}$, $11.0\times10^{-8}$, $24.75\times10^{-8}$ mol dm$^{-3}$s$^{-1}$ respectively. The order for the decomposition of AB is
questions.explanation: Doubling [AB] quadruples the rate ($11.0/2.75=4=2^2$), so the order is 2.

questions.q: The rate equation for a reaction : A $\to$ B is r = K[A]$^0$. If the initial concentration of the reactant is a mol dm$^{-3}$, the half life period of the reaction is
questions.explanation: For a zero-order reaction, $t_{1/2} = a/(2K)$.

questions.q: 30 cc of $\dfrac{M}{3}$ HCl, 20 cc of $\dfrac{M}{2}$ HNO$_3$ and 40 cc of $\dfrac{M}{4}$ NaOH solutions are mixed and the volume was made up to 1 dm$^3$. The pH of the resulting solution is
questions.explanation: Moles: HCl=0.01, HNO$_3$=0.01 (total acid 0.02), NaOH=0.01; excess acid = 0.01 mol in 1 L gives [H$^+$]=0.01 M, so pH = 2.

questions.q: An aqueous solution containing 6.5 gm of NaCl of 90% purity was subjected to electrolysis. After the complete electrolysis, the solution was evaporated to get solid NaOH. The volume of 1 M acetic acid required to neutralise NaOH obtained above is
questions.explanation: Pure NaCl = 5.85 g = 0.1 mol, which on electrolysis gives 0.1 mol NaOH; volume of 1 M acetic acid needed = 0.1 mol / 1 M = 100 cm$^3$.

questions.q: The standard electrode potential for the half cell reactions are: Zn$^{++}$ + 2e$^-$ $\longrightarrow$ Zn, E° = $-0.76$ V; Fe$^{++}$ + 2e$^-$ $\longrightarrow$ Fe, E° = $-0.44$ V. The E.M.F. of the cell reaction : Fe$^{++}$ + Zn $\longrightarrow$ Zn$^{++}$ + Fe is
$10^{-6}$ M NaOH is diluted 100 times. The pH of the diluted base is
questions.explanation: Diluting to $10^{-8}$ M NaOH, the contribution from water's autoionisation dominates, giving a pH just above 7, i.e. between 7 and 8.

questions.q: In the electrolysis of acidulated water, it is desired to obtain 1.12 cc of Hydrogen per second under S.T.P. condition. The current to be passed is
The one which decreases with dilution is
questions.explanation: Specific conductance decreases on dilution as ion concentration per unit volume falls, while molar/equivalent conductance increase.

questions.q: Vapour pressure of pure 'A' is 70 mm of Hg at 25 °C. It forms an ideal solution with 'B' in which mole fraction of A is 0.8. If the vapour pressure of the solution is 84 mm of Hg at 25 °C, the vapour pressure of pure 'B' at 25 °C is
questions.explanation: By Raoult's law, $84 = 70(0.8) + P_B^0(0.2) = 56 + 0.2P_B^0 \Rightarrow P_B^0 = 140$ mm.

questions.q: A 6% solution of urea is isotonic with
questions.explanation: 6% urea (M=60) = 60 g/L = 1 M; isotonic solutions of non-electrolytes have equal molar concentration, i.e. 1 M glucose.

questions.q: In countries nearer to polar region, the roads are sprinkled with CaCl$_2$. This is
options: to minimise the accumulation of dust on the road
to minimise the wear and tear of the roads
questions.explanation: CaCl$_2$ actually works by depressing the freezing point of ice/snow (a colligative effect) so it melts faster; none of the listed options state this correctly, which is why KEA awarded a grace mark.

questions.q: For the reaction H$_2$O (l) $\rightleftharpoons$ H$_2$O(g) at 373 K and one atmospheric pressure
questions.explanation: At the normal boiling point the liquid and vapour are in equilibrium, so $\Delta G=0$, which gives $\Delta H = T\Delta S$.

questions.q: A compound of 'A' and 'B' crystallises in a cubic lattice in which the 'A' atoms occupy the lattice points at the corners of the cube. The 'B' atoms occupy the centre of each face of the cube. The probable empirical formula of the compound is
questions.explanation: Corner atoms contribute $8\times1/8=1$ A per unit cell; face-centred atoms contribute $6\times1/2=3$ B per unit cell, giving AB$_3$.

questions.q: In electrophillic aromatic substitution reaction, the nitro group is meta directing because it
options: increases electron density at meta position
increases electron density at ortho and para positions
decreases electron density at ortho and para positions
decreases electron density at meta position
questions.explanation: The strongly electron-withdrawing -NO$_2$ group decreases electron density at the ortho and para positions (by resonance and induction), leaving the meta position comparatively favoured for electrophilic attack.

questions.q: CH$_3$COOH $\xrightarrow{\text{LiAlH}_4}$ X $\xrightarrow[300°C]{\text{Cu}}$ Y $\xrightarrow{\text{dilute NaOH}}$ Z. In the above reaction Z is
questions.explanation: CH$_3$COOH is reduced to ethanol (X), dehydrogenated over Cu to acetaldehyde (Y), which undergoes aldol condensation with dilute NaOH to give aldol (Z).

questions.q: The best method for the conversion of an alcohol into an alkyl chloride is by treating the alcohol with
options: Dry HCl in the presence of anhydrous ZnCl$_2$
questions.explanation: SOCl$_2$ with pyridine gives clean alkyl chloride with only gaseous SO$_2$ and HCl byproducts, avoiding rearrangement.

questions.q: The electrophile involved in the sulphonation of Benzene is
questions.explanation: In sulphonation of benzene with fuming sulphuric acid, the electrophile is SO$_3$.

questions.q: The carbon-carbon bond length in Benzene is
questions.explanation: Benzene's C-C bond length (~139 pm) lies between the single bond of ethane (154 pm) and the double bond of ethene (134 pm), due to delocalisation.

questions.q: The compound which is not formed during the dry distillation of a mixture of calcium formate and calcium acetate is
questions.explanation: Cross/self ketonic decarboxylation gives methanal (formate+formate), ethanal (formate+acetate) and propanone (acetate+acetate); propanal would need a propionate salt, which is absent.

questions.q: An organic compound X is oxidised by using acidified K$_2$Cr$_2$O$_7$. The product obtained reacts with Phenyl hydrazine but does not answer silver mirror test. The possible structure of X is
questions.explanation: A secondary alcohol like (CH$_3$)$_2$CHOH oxidises to a ketone (acetone), which reacts with phenylhydrazine but fails Tollen's (silver mirror) test, unlike aldehydes.

questions.q: The reaction involved in the oil of Winter Green test is Salicylic acid $\xrightarrow[\text{Conc. } H_2SO_4]{\Delta}$ product. The product is treated with Na$_2$CO$_3$ solution. The missing reagent in the above reaction is
questions.explanation: Salicylic acid esterifies with methanol (conc. H$_2$SO$_4$, heat) to give methyl salicylate, 'oil of wintergreen'.

questions.q: The compound which forms acetaldehyde when heated with dilute NaOH is
questions.explanation: The gem-dihalide CH$_3$CHCl$_2$ (1,1-dichloroethane) hydrolyses with dilute NaOH to give acetaldehyde.

questions.q: Arrange the following in the increasing order of their basic strengths : CH$_3$NH$_2$, (CH$_3$)$_2$NH, (CH$_3$)$_3$N, NH$_3$
questions.explanation: In aqueous solution, steric hindrance and poor solvation weaken (CH$_3$)$_3$N's basicity, giving the order NH$_3$ < (CH$_3$)$_3$N < CH$_3$NH$_2$ < (CH$_3$)$_2$NH.

questions.q: The one which has least Iodine value is
questions.explanation: Ghee is highly saturated fat with the least degree of unsaturation, giving it the lowest iodine value among the options.

questions.q: A diabetic person carries a pocket of Glucose with him always, because
options: Glucose reduces the blood sugar level.
Glucose increases the blood sugar level almost instantaneously.
Glucose reduces the blood sugar level slowly.
Glucose increases the blood sugar level slowly.
questions.explanation: Glucose is a simple sugar absorbed almost immediately, quickly raising blood sugar level during a hypoglycemic episode.

questions.q: There are 20 naturally occurring amino acids. The maximum number of tripeptides that can be obtained is
questions.explanation: Each of the 3 positions in a tripeptide can be any of the 20 amino acids (repetition allowed), giving $20^3 = 8000$.

questions.q: Cooking is fast in a pressure cooker, because
options: food is cooked at constant volume.
loss of heat due to radiation is minimum.
water boils at higher temperature inside the pressure cooker.
questions.explanation: Increased pressure inside the sealed cooker raises the boiling point of water, so cooking occurs at a higher temperature, speeding up cooking.
